* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPAC323.01c
https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000006109/


* **Description of issue**

The cerevisiae ortholog of SPAC323.01c is SGD:S000006109/POS5
This enzyme is specific for NADH and mitochondrion.

(https://www.embopress.org/doi/full/10.1093/emboj/cdg211 ) that although the recombinant protein has NAD+ kinase activity, it is 50x lower than the NADH kinase activity, and it has the opposite levels of NAD+/NADH activity as a known NAD+ kinase. The reference you provided shows that Pos5 prefers NADH over NAD+ and states:

“Previously, two forms of NAD+ kinase were detected in S. cerevisiae: a NADH-specific form was localized exclusively in mitochondria, and a NAD+-specific form was distributed in microsomal and cytosolic fractions ([24](https://journals.asm.org/doi/10.1128/ec.2.4.809-820.2003#core-collateral-R24)). Our observation of the same substrate specificity for the mitochondrial NADH kinase Pos5 implies that we have cloned and characterized the mitochondrial form of the enzyme originally described and partially purified by Iwahashi et al. ([24](https://journals.asm.org/doi/10.1128/ec.2.4.809-820.2003#core-collateral-R24)).”
